title: Meltdown Monday
one_liner: Defend a chain of supermarket freezers from overnight remote defrost attacks before the ice cream melts.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: Hackers remotely switched European supermarket freezers into defrost mode overnight, pushing temperatures up to 55°C across eight countries after an earlier wave in France. Controllers were sitting on the open internet.
demo: A night-time map shows 20 stores with live freezer thermometers. Simulated attacks hit internet-exposed controllers and temperatures climb. The visitor spends a limited budget on fixes (change default password, VPN, high-temp alarm, take offline) and watches spoiled-stock euros pile up for stores left exposed. At the end, a recap compares their losses with the real Belgian figure.
data_plan: Simulated attack timing and store data, clearly labelled. Real incident figures from the podcast appear in a sourced recap.
risks: Must not teach attack techniques. Keep defenses generic and attacks abstract.
